title: SYSK Selects: Are there undiscovered people?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the January 2010 episode "Are There Undiscovered People?" The hosts open by framing a 2008 news story (Independent coverage of aerial photos of bow-wielding people in Brazil) that called the group undiscovered, when they were actually known uncontacted or isolated people. They explain the terminology (undiscovered vs. uncontacted vs. isolated), the history of European colonization and slavery, maps that labeled unexplored lands with monsters, the Brazilian Akuntsu massacre by loggers and ranchers, the Sentinelese of the Andaman Islands, the threat of disease to uncontacted tribes, the roughly hundred uncontacted tribes concentrated in Brazil, Peru and Paraguay, government protection efforts, and the dangers of "savage tourism." The episode closes with listener mail about organ donation and anonymity between donors and recipients from an anesthesiologist.
topics: 2008 Independent newspaper photos of Brazilian tribe

segments.title: Rerun introduction
segments.summary: Josh introduces this Saturday Selects episode from January 2010 and hosts open with casual banter about the weather and Ghostbusters.

segments.title: 2008 undiscovered tribe news photos
segments.summary: The hosts discuss newspaper coverage of aerial photos from a low-flying helicopter showing bow-wielding people in Brazil, described as undiscovered. Chuck says the coverage was overblown, since the group was known and followed for years by an Indian expert.

segments.title: Can anyone be undiscovered today?
segments.summary: The hosts argue it is nearly impossible to be truly undiscovered given GPS and heat sensors, but some people still live isolated and primitive lives. They explain the shifting terms undiscovered, uncontacted and isolated, and note that these groups want no contact.

segments.title: Colonization, slavery and early maps
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the history of enslaving newly encountered peoples, including Columbus and the Arawak, comparisons with African and Roman slavery, and old maps that marked unexplored lands with monsters.

segments.title: Akuntsu massacre and disease threats
segments.summary: The hosts describe how the Akuntsu in Brazil were attacked by loggers and ranchers, with most of the tribe killed and only a few surviving, and discuss disease, including 1980s missionary contact with the Zoe and a 1996 illegal logger contact with the Maroon tribe.

segments.title: Sentinelese and government protection
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Sentinelese of the Andaman Islands, who are relatively uncontacted and not threatened, and discuss protections in Brazil, Peru's oil-related conflicts, and Paraguay revoking a ranching license. They also mention savage tourism.

segments.title: Learning more and closing thoughts on respect
segments.summary: The hosts reflect on dismissing uncontacted peoples as savages and suggest the HowStuffWorks site for further reading on people.

segments.title: Sponsor thanks and mugs
segments.summary: Thanks to Dan of Dan Made pottery for coffee mugs and a note about other listener gifts.

segments.title: Organ donation anonymity
segments.summary: Listener Todd, an anesthesiologist specializing in liver and kidney transplants, explains that donors and recipients usually do not meet for about a year, that identifying information is censored, and that people can still find each other via websites though it is discouraged.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and invite listeners to write in.
